title: Canonical closed-test derived exchange and restriction maps
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], and use the exact internal-module inverse images and ordinary unbounded total derived direct images [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], with the size convention [def-weil-size-convention]. Write $P_f=f^*$ for the termwise derived inverse image, $R_f=Rf_*$, and use their canonical derived adjunction. For $f:X\to Y$, $g:Y\to Z$, let $c_{f,g}:P_{g\circ f}\simeq P_fP_g$ be canonical pullback composition. For a commutative square $h:T\to X$, $q:T\to Z$, $f:X\to U$, $s:Z\to U$, let $P_qP_s\simeq P_hP_f$ be the comparison induced by composition and $fh=sq$. Define $\mathrm{Ex}:P_sR_f\to R_qP_h$ as its canonical adjunction mate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-square-exchange].
Let $\Gamma_Y$ be the internal-module global sections functor [def-sfb-condensed-module-sections]. Define $d_f:R\Gamma_Y R_f\simeq R\Gamma_X$ by the canonical derived composition comparison normalized by the ordinary section identity $\Gamma_Yf_*=\Gamma_X$. Define $\rho_f:R\Gamma_Y\to R\Gamma_XP_f$ as the derived $f$-unit followed by $d_f$. For $b:W\to X$, put $S_b=R\Gamma_WP_b$. For $a:W'\to W$, define $S_b\to S_{ba}$ by $P_b\rho_a$ and pullback composition; if $ba=b'$, transport its target to $S_{b'}$. For a square as above with lower edge $b:W\to U$ and upper edge $h:T\to X$, define the section comparison $S_bR_f\to S_h$ by applying $R\Gamma_W$ to $\mathrm{Ex}$ and then $P_h d_q$.
Fix a commutative ring $A$, an ideal $I$, $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$, and $s:Z=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)\to U$ the quotient-induced closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. For $V\to Z$ in the affine ind-etale basis [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-basis], let $W=v(V)$ and $i_V:V\to W$ be the canonical closed-lift inclusion [def-exc-closed-site-lift]. Define the closed comparison $S_{W\to U}\to S_{V\to Z}P_s$ as restriction along $i_V$, transported by $i_V(W\to U)=s(V\to Z)$ and pullback composition. For a commutative square $(h,f_Z,f,s)$ define $T=X\times_UW$, $T_0=X_Z\times_ZV$ [def-pc-fibre-product], and $a:T_0\to T$ by the projections $h\operatorname{pr}_1$ and $i_V\operatorname{pr}_2$. Define test restriction $S_{T\to X}\to S_{T_0\to X_Z}P_h$ as restriction along $a$ followed by the projection equality and pullback composition. The evaluated exchange is $\mathrm{Ex}$ followed by $S_{V\to Z}$.
For maps of tests $a:W'\to W$ over $U$, the fibre map $X\times_UW'\to X\times_UW$ is defined by the pullback universal property. Define $\mathrm{TestNaturality}$ to be the proposition that the section comparison commutes with these restriction maps at every bounded-below derived input. All these constructions use the actual units, counits, composition isomorphisms and pullback maps; they assert no invertibility of exchange or restriction, and require no affine, qcqs, proper or finite-presentation hypothesis on the source and no weak-contractibility hypothesis on the tests.
